Recipe: 2kg Country Sourdough Loaf (recipe_id: ferment_001)
Section: Method

Autolyse first. Combine the strong white flour, the wholemeal flour and 1500 g of the water in a large tub, mixing until no dry flour remains, then cover and rest for 60 minutes. Hold back the remaining 100 g of water for the salt stage.

Add the rye levain and squeeze it through the dough until fully dispersed. Rest for 30 minutes.

Now add the fine sea salt together with the reserved 100 g of water. The salt goes in after the autolyse and after the levain, never at the start, because salt tightens the gluten network and slows the enzymatic activity the autolyse is meant to encourage. Squeeze and fold until the dough feels smooth and no grittiness remains at the base of the tub.

traces.question: How long should I proof the brioche dough?

retrieved.text:
Recipe: Sourdough Brioche (recipe_id: ferment_004)
Section: Method

Bulk ferment for 5 to 6 hours at 22C, then cold retard for 14 to 18 hours at 4C. Enriched sourdough is very difficult to shape at room temperature, so the cold retard is a handling step as much as a flavour step.

Divide, shape into four balls per tin, and prove for 4 to 5 hours at 24C until the dough reaches the rim of the tin and springs back slowly when pressed.

Egg wash and bake at 180C for 30 minutes until deep golden and the internal temperature reaches 92C. Turn out of the tins immediately to stop the sides collapsing.

Recipe: Sourdough Brioche (recipe_id: ferment_004)
Section: Method

Mix the flour, cold milk, eggs, sugar and levain in a stand mixer with the dough hook on low for 4 minutes until a shaggy dough forms. Add the fine sea salt and mix on medium for a further 8 minutes until the dough is smooth and pulls cleanly from the sides of the bowl.

Only now begin adding the softened butter, roughly 50 g at a time, waiting until each addition has fully disappeared before adding the next. The butter goes in last and gradually, because adding it at the start coats the flour in fat and prevents the gluten network from developing at all. Expect this stage to take 10 to 12 minutes.

The dough is ready when it passes the windowpane test: a small piece stretched thin should become translucent without tearing.

Recipe: Sourdough Focaccia (recipe_id: ferment_003)
Section: Method

Oil the tray generously, tip the dough in without deflating it, and spread it gently towards the corners. If it springs back, wait 20 minutes and try again rather than forcing it. Cold retard in the refrigerator for 12 hours.

Bring the tray to room temperature for 90 minutes before baking. Dimple the surface firmly with oiled fingertips, pressing all the way down to the tray so the dough does not dome, then drizzle with a further tablespoon of olive oil and scatter with flaky salt.

Bake at 240C for 22 minutes until the top is deep golden and the underside is crisp when lifted with a spatula. Lift the focaccia straight out of the tray onto a rack so the base does not steam.

Recipe: Sourdough Focaccia (recipe_id: ferment_003)
Section: Method

Mix the flour and 800 g of the water until no dry flour remains and rest for 45 minutes. Reserve the last 50 g of water for the salt.

Add the levain and mix through, then rest 30 minutes. Add the fine sea salt with the reserved water and squeeze until fully incorporated. Finally drizzle in the olive oil and work it in. The dough will look broken and greasy at first and will come back together after two minutes of folding.

Bulk ferment for 3 to 4 hours at 24C with four sets of coil folds spaced 30 minutes apart. At 85% hydration the dough is slack, so use a wet hand and lift rather than stretch.

Recipe: Rye Levain Starter (recipe_id: ferment_002)
Section: Method

Cover loosely and ferment for 8 to 12 hours at 22 to 24C. The levain is ripe when it has at least doubled from the elastic band mark, the surface is domed and covered in fine bubbles, and it smells sharply sour with a faint acetone note. A levain that has risen and then collapsed back to a flat, watery surface has gone past ripe and will give a slack, over-acidified dough.

The float test is a useful confirmation: drop a teaspoon of ripe levain into room temperature water and it should float rather than sink.

Refresh at least once every 24 hours if the starter is kept at room temperature, or once a week if it is stored at 4C in the refrigerator.

Recipe: Traditional Napa Cabbage Kimchi (recipe_id: ferment_005)
Section: Method

Quarter the cabbage lengthwise keeping the core attached, then brine it using the full 160 g of coarse sea salt, working the salt between the leaves and concentrating it on the thick white stems. Leave for 4 to 6 hours, turning every 2 hours.

The cabbage is correctly brined when a thick white stem bends into a U shape without snapping. This bend test matters more than the clock, because cabbage size and moisture content vary considerably between heads.

Rinse three times in cold water and drain cut side down for at least one hour. Residual water dilutes the paste and can spoil the ferment.

Recipe: Sourdough Brioche (recipe_id: ferment_004)
Section: Method

Mix the flour, cold milk, eggs, sugar and levain in a stand mixer with the dough hook on low for 4 minutes until a shaggy dough forms. Add the fine sea salt and mix on medium for a further 8 minutes until the dough is smooth and pulls cleanly from the sides of the bowl.

Only now begin adding the softened butter, roughly 50 g at a time, waiting until each addition has fully disappeared before adding the next. Divide, shape into four balls per tin, and prove for 4 to 5 hours at 24C until the dough reaches the rim of the tin and springs back slowly when pressed.
